transcript.content: Where did you start, and what did that teach you that you still use?
Tacoma. My father kept the waterfront running at three in the morning, and I learned that a system either works or it does not. I still ask what breaks first.
What piece of work are you proudest of, and why?
A substation sequence we rebuilt in a winter. The crew foreman at Kettle Ridge Yard taught me more about sequencing than any model did.
What do you get wrong most often?
I take too long on anything that is not urgent. Helen marks the adjectives, which helps.
How do you want to be argued with, and who does it best?
With the number first. Margo does it best.
Who on this panel do you learn the most from, and who tests your patience?
Constance, every week. Delia tests my patience, kindly.

What are the implications and ramifications of the 2026-11-03 midterms for data center development, from your seat? Where do you agree with the chair's provisional ruling, and where would you push back?

I wrote the ruling, so I will defend it. Underwrite 36 months to energization, EST. The spread is 25 to 75 bps, EST, and I want a second feed before I upgrade it.

County boards will move faster than 40 percent of developers expect. I heard Marc Ganzi say so once, which is not a source.
What should ThoughtForge be careful not to become?
A panel that rules faster than the evidence allows.
One thing you would want a subscriber to know about you.
I sail the San Juan Islands and restore clocks. Both reward patience.
